title: floor vs lower
options: floor(4) = 4, lower(4) = 2 — floor is inclusive, lower is strict
explanation: floor = largest element ≤ x (can be x itself); lower = largest element < x. Same distinction for ceiling vs higher.

title: Navigation calls
prompt: Fill in the TreeMap navigation for 'most recent snapshot at or before time t'.
explanation: This exact floorKey-then-null-check is the core of Time Based Key-Value Store (a NeetCode problem).

title: Recall: ends of a TreeMap
code:
int lo = tm.{{1}}();                          // 1 — smallest key
int hi = tm.{{2}}();                          // 9 — largest key
Map.Entry<Integer, String> e = tm.{{3}}();    // returns 1=a AND removes it
int next = tm.firstKey();                     // now 5
explanation: `firstKey`/`lastKey` read the extremes without changing the map. `pollFirstEntry` returns the smallest entry and removes it, so the next `firstKey` is 5. (`firstEntry` would return 1=a but leave it in place.)

title: Closest value
prompt: Return the value in `nums` closest to `target` (ties go to the smaller value). Load a TreeSet, then compare `floor(target)` and `ceiling(target)` — remember either can be null.

solution.explanation: The two candidates bracket the target; null-checks first, then compare distances with <= so ties pick the smaller (floor) side.

hints: Only two candidates matter: floor and ceiling.

title: Recall: TreeSet navigation
code:
TreeSet<Integer> ts = new TreeSet<>();
ts.{{1}}(5);               // insert
Integer lo = ts.{{2}}(4);  // largest element <= 4
Integer hi = ts.{{3}}(4);  // smallest element >= 4
int f = ts.{{4}}();        // smallest element
explanation: `floor(x)` = largest ≤ x, `ceiling(x)` = smallest ≥ x (both can be null); `first()` is the minimum.

title: Drill: smallest at least x
prompt: From memory: load `nums` into a TreeSet and return the smallest value ≥ `x` (its `ceiling`), or `-1` if none exists.

solution.explanation: `ceiling(x)` walks the sorted tree in O(log n) and returns `null` when every element is below `x`, hence the null check before unboxing.

title: Recall: TreeMap navigation
prompt: Fill in the sorted-map key operations.
code:
TreeMap<Integer, String> tm = new TreeMap<>();
tm.{{1}}(3, "c");            // insert
Integer k = tm.{{2}}(5);     // largest key <= 5
Integer h = tm.{{3}}(5);     // smallest key >= 5
explanation: `floorKey`/`ceilingKey` mirror TreeSet's floor/ceiling but return keys — the heart of Time Based Key-Value Store.

title: Drill: largest key at most q
prompt: From memory: put every value of `keys` into a TreeMap (value → itself as a String), then return the largest key ≤ `q` (`floorKey`), or `-1` if none.

solution.explanation: `floorKey(q)` finds the largest key ≤ q in O(log n); it returns `null` when every key is greater than q, so check before unboxing.
